name: Little Nightmares
short_description: A small child in a raincoat sneaks through a giant, grotesque ship.
sources: oracle study 2026-10-23 (public knowledge, no store fetch, no game files)
summary: A small child in a raincoat sneaks through a giant, grotesque ship.

identity.core_loop: Sneak, climb, hide, solve a small physical puzzle, run from a giant, reach the next room.
identity.ui_and_game_feel: Tense and tactile; you feel small against everything.

hud_coverage.method: Oracle study from public knowledge of the game, in our own words; not yet measured on capture

information_grammar.note: No HUD at all: a lighter in the dark, footsteps and the giants' bodies tell you everything.

identity.art_direction: Dollhouse diorama seen from the side, dark with warm pools of light.

rendering.source: derived from the art note by rendering_notes.RULES

tricks: A small state machine (idle, start, move) with designer-swappable override slots, so wading, ash and water reuse one set at new speeds
Ability sets combine (holding hands while wading) without new code
Monsters are built on one exaggerated trait each (a long neck, walking on the ceiling) and scripted with the state machine
motion.lesson: Override slots let one child walk through many grounds; give each giant one exaggerated way of moving.

sources.title: Unreal Engine interview: how Little Nightmares II plumbs the depths of adolescent angst

motion.source: oracle motion study 2026-10-23 (public talks, interviews and breakdowns; no game files)

identity.audio_mood: Low drones, creaks, music box moments.
identity.lessons_for_abbies_world: A dollhouse side view and no HUD at all; size alone tells you you are small. Kid-safe only in its framing, not its horror.
